newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Crimea launches bond worth $63 mln.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Crimea launches bond worth $63 mln.

text.p: The local government of Ukraine's Crimean peninsula launched a bond worth 120 million hryvnia ($63 million) on November 28, the region's prime minister told Reuters on Tuesday.
Commercial banks have already offered to take up 100 million hryvnias of the one-year bonds, whose denomination is 100 hryvnias, he added.
But Arkady Demidenko said bonds worth only 10 million hryvnias had actually been sold so far.
The Crimean Finance Ministry will pay annual interest worth 70 percent of the Ukrainian Central Bank's refinancing levels, which are 40 percent. Payments will be made monthly.
Non-residents can buy Crimean bonds through Ukrainian commercial banks. Crimea issued its first bond, worth 5 million hryvnias, in the middle of the year.
